metadata.title: ORCHID literature values
metadata.description:
ORCHID literature values: thermodynamic and phase-equilibrium values read from published papers, each stored as an observation of an equilibrium state (quantity, phases, temperature, pressure, phase compositions, reference state) with its evidence class, source paper and DOI, page, and the table row or verbatim sentence it was read from. Part of the ORCHID data release v2026.10 (Open Repository for CALPHAD Hypotheses, Intelligence, and Discovery).

Status. Version 1, machine-extracted: values were read from papers by language-model readers constrained to quote their source and checked automatically (quote verification, field-placement rule, printed-page sign checks, DFT and Kim et al. 2017 cross-checks); a hand-checked precision sample is in progress.

What

  • 76,432 values from 1,322 papers covering 1,390 chemical systems; 75,491 accepted (reader agreement plus deterministic checks).
  • Evidence classes, never mixed or averaged: experimental 36,918, model 28,148 (CALPHAD or other models; 13,586 linked to the exact TDB file by SHA-256), DFT 6,162, unspecified 5,204.
  • Invariant reactions 26,423, phase transitions 10,201, phase equilibria 5,847, formation quantities 13,024, crystal structure 9,428, and heat capacity, entropy, mixing, activity and EMF values.
  • Bibliography of 4,877 reporting papers and cited works; experimental context (samples, heat treatments, measurements) of 225 papers, each item with its quote and page.
  • Formats: JSON per chemical system (literature/systems/), full JSONL.gz and CSV.gz dumps, Parquet tables (literature_values with a by-paper train/validation/test split, papers, experimental_context); fields documented in literature/SCHEMA.md, datasheet in DATASET_CARD.md.

How

Tables and passages of lawfully held papers were read independently by language-model readers (Gemini Flash, Claude Opus, Gemini Pro for confirmation) and the PDF text layer; a value is accepted only on reader agreement plus deterministic checks: quote verification (the sentence must be verbatim on one page and contain the printed value), the field-placement rule (fields not printed in the quote or row are dropped), printed-page sign checks of formation enthalpies, and cross-checks against DFT (Materials Project, OQMD) and Kim et al. 2017. 3,510 exact duplicates were merged; reaction types and property codes mapped to controlled vocabularies; every correction is listed with its evidence in literature/QUALITY_FIXES.md.

Limitations

  • Version 1 is machine-extracted; a hand-checked precision sample is in progress.
  • Values in figures are not included; coverage across systems is uneven.
  • 2,765 formation values have a per-atom vs per-formula basis the paper does not state (unit kJ/mol (basis unstated), not converted); 2,680 are per atom only by a magnitude heuristic.
  • Uncertainties with basis stated_default or reading_resolution are placeholders, not measurements.
  • experimental values cited from older work carry the citing paper's reading; unspecified values may be experimental or calculated; check flag_source_disputed, flag_magnitude_suspect and flag_system_mismatch before use.
  • flag_espei_ready marks a fully specified state, not a review verdict: do not feed values to an optimizer without review.

Licence

ORCHID's data are released under CC BY 4.0, as are the SGTE (B. Hallstedt, Calphad 89 (2025) 102833), Materials Project and OQMD data from which they are derived; attributions and statements of changes are in NOTICE.md, the licence of each folder in LICENSES.md (both in the bundle). The quotations from papers that accompany values are short excerpts kept for verification; they remain under the publishers' copyright and are not relicensed. Source papers, page images and full texts are not redistributed.

Files: one zip (orchid-literature-v2026.10.zip) holding the files at their repository paths, a MANIFEST.sha256, the README, CHANGELOG and licence files. Its file list with sizes and SHA-256 is zenodo/literature.files.json in the data repository.

How to cite

R. Arróyave, J. Saal, D. Shin, ORCHID literature values (version 2026.10; Version 1, machine-extracted), Zenodo (2026). https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.PENDING-literature

Part of: R. Arróyave, J. Saal, D. Shin, ORCHID data (version 2026.10; Version 1, machine-extracted), Zenodo (2026). https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.PENDING-orchid-data

Also cite the original source of every value you use (paper_citation / paper_doi, and cited_dois for values the paper cites from earlier work).
